restrictions: The two messages have 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 bytes for one t with 1 <= t < 2^32: t zero chunks of 1024 bytes followed by a last chunk of one block. The last chunk is compressed as a non-root chunk with counter t (v12 = t, v13 = 0), flags 3 and its true block length; the 63-byte block ends in eight zero bytes, so words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero in both zero-filled blocks. Equal last-chunk chaining values give equal digests by the tree lemma of proof.md Section 7.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every trial of proof.md Section 8 the two last-chunk chaining values agree on words 0, 2, 5 and 7, E1.c1 lies in the cube of beta* = 18b0e098, Y4 is held in the sub-class of 131,072 values, and the counter t is solved per trial as ROL(K0.d1,16) XOR K0.a1; trials with t = 0 are dropped. For a frame (six outer words and Y4) a 32-bit word K(D2.a1), computed by 29 assignments, equals an explicit word H(E1.d1, E1.a2) for every trial (Lemma AK, from GPT Sol's answer AK). One table of the 2^32 values of D2.a1 per frame returns every root of a query, and a fixed table of 53 * 2^26 E1 records lists every (c1, E1.a2) with one of the seven E1 outcomes of beta*, so the search forms exactly the E1-listed trials of each frame and certifies exactly its listed good trials (Lemmas KT and TG). Heuristic part: over 228,885,859,807 frames, 2^90.736 trials covered, a collision is found with probability at least 0.40 under H1', H7' and H8'.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5, 430 machine units (operations, loads, stores) per unit, 16 registers; every load is one unit wherever its word lies. Allowances in words from GPT Sol's answer AK, not counted by a program: per frame 4,096 for the random word and 35 frame lines, 512 per value of D2.a1 for the table (2^32 values), 64 per E1 record scanned (53 * 2^26 records); 8,192 per returned root for its reconstruction, the tests of Q*, t and rule A and two last-chunk compressions; 2^46 once for the E1 record table. The run halts with failure after 228,885,859,807 frames or when the returned roots exceed 7,950,139,765,405,122,560; every row is charged at its count or cap. With the selection procedure in full, O_tot = 1,119,513,944,455,286,104,385,416 operations, T <= O_tot/430 + 2^38, log2 T = 71.1410 (proof.md Sections 9, 11).

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word per frame. The success probability 0.40 (bound 0.40012) holds only under H1' (rate at 5/7 of the model's conditional count, a margin of 1.40 where earlier entries on this track used half; at half the time_log2 would be 71.45), H7' (clustering of the good trials of a frame of 2^53 trials) and H8' (mean number of E1-listed trials per frame at most 53 * 2^15). None is measured. The organizer-run experiments run the root instance of the same construction (counter 0, flags 11), because no digest experiment can show a half-collision of a non-root chunk's chaining value. No full 2-round collision is exhibited and none was computed. The search of proof.md Section 9 is defined in the text only and has not been implemented; the submitted program contains steps CO and CT, the compression and the rule A test that it uses.

Six 32-bit constants, the word eta, two bits of the sub-class, three 32-bit constants of the rule test, the beta* cube and the seven tau values with eps are stored in the program (92 bytes of advice). The constants were found by a participant's solver search and chosen by a participant's count; the sub-class and rule A were proposed by GPT Sol 6.1 from exact counts that the participant's counter reproduces. preprocessing_log2 70 bounds the selection procedure of proof.md Section 12 and the E1 record table and is included in time_log2; the per-frame tables are built in the search and charged in time_log2. memory_log2_bytes 44 covers the two output messages (each below 2^42 bytes), the code, the selection procedure and the search (below 2^39 bytes: the E1 record table and one frame table, 388,694,540,288 bytes), all held at once. No priority or novelty claim is made.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. For an outer step of the counter construction whose seven outer words are independent uniform 32-bit words and whose member y is uniform in the sub-class of 131,072 values, let N_o be the number of its listed good valid trials over all of the cube Q* of beta* = 18b0e098: t != 0, equal last-chunk chaining values (R = 0), rule A, and an E1 outcome among the seven outcomes of beta*. Assume E[N_o] >= (2^21 - 1) q with q = (5/7) p = 5 * 1033 / (7 * 2^101), about 2^-91.473, where p = 1033 * 2^-101 is the conditional model rate of Lemma S1. A frame of the search (six outer words and y drawn uniformly, D2.a1 over all 2^32 values) has W = the sum of N_o over its outer steps, so E[W] = 2^32 E[N_o] >= 2^32 (2^21 - 1) q, about 2^-38.473, and the run's 228,885,859,807 frames give FRAMES * E[W] >= 0.6. This is a first-moment statement only: it asserts neither independent trials nor independent uniform E1 or E3 words. It is the premise H-AK-rate of GPT Sol's answer AK, the rate premise of the earlier counter searches regrouped by frames (proof.md 10.3).
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Sections 8 and 9: lengths 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 with a non-root last chunk (counter t < 2^32, v13 = 0, flags 3), the six constants of Section 3.2, Y4 in the sub-class of 131,072 values, E1.c1 in Q*, t solved per trial and t = 0 dropped, outer words and member drawn from the run's fresh 256-bit words. W counts all of Q* and all values of D2.a1 in each frame; the search certifies exactly these trials (Lemma TG).
heuristics.extrapolation: From the participant's exact count, in integer arithmetic under the seven-word model, of the beta* part of the sub-class kept by rule A (seven outcomes, 67,698,688 = 1033 * 2^16; the counting program and its output are printed in Section 17), times 2^11 for drawing E1.c1 from the cube (Lemma S1: conditioning the model on the cube leaves the E3 side unchanged), taken at 5/7, a margin of 1.40 chosen by the participant; entry e7b17fd1 and the earlier entries on this track took half. Regrouping the outer steps into frames does not change the mean, by linearity. Participant evidence of Section 13, untrusted by the harness: 2^45.6 real 32-bit counter trials whose measurable partial events match the exact model within about 1% to about 2^-31.7, and a reduced-width (8-bit) end-to-end run of complete messages in which the counter arrangement found 251 collisions against 255.0 predicted. The joint 128-bit event itself, about 2^-91 per trial, is not measured at 32 bits.
heuristics.limitations: The factor (5/7) * 138,646,913,024 = 99,033,509,302.86 per 2^128 is assumed; at 5/7 this premise is stronger than the half-count premise of the earlier entries and is not implied by it (at half the count the same search is priced at time_log2 71.45). The organizer-run experiments run the root instance (counter 0, flags 11) and measure neither the factor nor the counter half-collision. The transfer of the single-trial law to the construction is partly proved (Lemmas S1 to S4 and IP) and partly assumed here; the share of the success mass carried by the dropped member with t = 0 is not bounded. No measurement of this premise exists at its scale, and the workload validation made for another search of this construction does not bear on it.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. For a frame of the search of proof.md Section 9 (the six outer words C0.d1, D2.b1, S11, S4, X9, w6 and a member y of the sub-class, drawn uniformly), let W count all listed good valid trials over all 2^32 values of D2.a1 and all 2^21 members of Q* (t != 0, R = 0, rule A, an E1 outcome among the seven of beta*). Assume E[W (W - 1)] <= 0.0065 E[W]. With H1' and the independence of the frames, Lemma S8 then bounds by exp(-0.6 * (1 - 0.0065 / 2)) = exp(-0.59805) < 0.549883 the probability that no frame of the run has W > 0. This is the premise H-AK-cluster of GPT Sol's answer AK.
heuristics.scope: The frames of the run: groups of 2^53 trials that share Y4, Y12 and w5 (Lemma AK (a)), with Y9 and w8 shared within each of their 2^32 outer steps. Pairs of good trials in different outer steps of one frame are included.
heuristics.extrapolation: None measured. The bound 0.0065 is the value used on this track for the dependence of the good trials of one outer step; here it is applied to a group 2^32 times larger, and GPT Sol (answer AK) states that it is a new premise, implied neither by premises on outer steps or aligned groups nor by the reduced-width toy runs. Differences between frames in their mean enter E[W (W - 1)] only through the square of a mean of about 2^-38.47 per frame, so they matter only if extreme; what would break the premise is a mechanism by which the good trials of one frame come in pairs or groups, and none is known or excluded.
heuristics.limitations: No proof and no measurement at any size: no scaled-down run of the frame search exists, and the workload validation made for another search of this construction does not apply. Lemma S7 bounds the successes of one outer step by 3,072, which gives no useful bound for a frame. Single outer steps of the counter arrangement differ strongly in partial events (a variance 572 times the mean for rule A), and the rate of a listed tau of E1 is a property of Y12 and w5, which a frame fixes. If the ratio rho is larger the bound falls: by Lemma S8 the success bound is 1 - exp(-0.6 b(rho)) - 0.05, which is 0.209 at rho = 1.

heuristics.statement: Supporting. For a frame of the search of proof.md Section 9, let N_r be the number of roots that the queries of its step 3 return, that is its number of E1-listed trials: trials with E1.c1 in Q* and an E1 outcome among the seven outcomes of beta*, counted before E3, t != 0 and rule A are tested (Lemma TG). Assume E[N_r] <= 53 * 2^15 = 1,736,704. With the root cap 20 * 228,885,859,807 * 1,736,704 = 7,950,139,765,405,122,560, Markov's inequality then bounds by 1/20 the probability that the run halts at the cap, with no independence assumed inside a frame. This is the premise H-AK-E1-work of GPT Sol's answer AK.
heuristics.scope: Every frame of the run; the count includes every returned root, whatever the E3 side, t and rule A of its trial.
heuristics.extrapolation: The product-model count: under the seven-word model, with E1.c1 uniform in Q* and E1.b1, E1.a2 uniform, a trial is E1-listed with probability sum L_j / 2^85 = 53 * 2^-38 (L_j of proof.md 10.1, which the record counts of 9.6 reproduce), and a frame has 2^53 trials with E1.c1 in Q*. Not measured: the nearest participant measurement, the listed E1 outcome on 2^45 real counter trials (real against model 1.009 +- 0.017, Section 13), is a larger event (model 10,176.0 against 6,784 for the seven outcomes) at the level of single trials, not of frames. The workload validation (gamma 38) made for another search of this construction does not apply to this algorithm (GPT Sol, answer AK).
heuristics.limitations: The physical transfer of the product-model count is open: in a frame Y12 and w5 are fixed, and the rate of a listed tau of E1 is known to depend on them strongly; the premise concerns the mean over frames only. No implementation of the frame search exists, so the number of roots of a real frame has never been counted. If the mean is larger, the time bound is unchanged, since the run halts at the cap, and the success bound falls by the probability of reaching it.
